Choosing the right itinerary requires distinguishing a brief sightseeing visit from a full travel stage, and accounting for re-entry into Argentina, connections and changing climates.

## Bolivia and Uruguay: two very different regions on one itinerary

**Uruguay and Bolivia are far apart and share no border.** Uruguay lies on the Atlantic coast and the Rio de la Plata estuary, while Bolivia's best-known travel destinations are high in the Andes. [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) offers walks through a port city, historic squares and waterfronts. [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) means traveling across a vast salt flat and volcanic landscapes, where altitude and weather play a major role.

The contrast is what makes this combination attractive, but it rarely fits into a short vacation. Here you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with both countries on their main route. **We have brought together all matching multi-country itineraries, not necessarily tours limited to Bolivia and Uruguay.** First examine the entire route, the number of overnight stays and the border crossings, then decide whether the time allocated to each country meets your needs.

On the published [32-day Ada Tours itinerary through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), travelers visit Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia. Uruguay is **a day trip from Buenos Aires, returning to the same city that evening**. Bolivia is a separate, multi-day mountain stage after Chile. The difference in how much time is spent in each country is essential when choosing the trip.

## How the visit to Uruguay works

### Montevideo from Buenos Aires: round-trip ferry

On day 9, **October 30, 2026**, the itinerary provides an early transfer to the port of [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), a ferry across the Rio de la Plata and a tour of Montevideo. Travelers visit the port, Independence Square, the city center, the Old Town and the Cathedral. The excursion is accompanied by an **English-speaking guide**. Free time follows before the return ferry, after which guests arrive back in Buenos Aires and transfer to their hotel.

**There is no overnight stay in Uruguay on this itinerary.** This is a convenient way to see its capital while based in Argentina, but it is not equivalent to a holiday on the Uruguayan coast or a journey through the country's interior. If you want Punta del Este, Colonia del Sacramento or a few relaxed days by the ocean, these places and additional time would have to be arranged separately. They are not listed as included visits in the current itinerary.

Ferry tickets are included. Nevertheless, the international water crossing takes time for boarding procedures and border control. It is important to know **both** departure times: the morning sailing from Argentina and the evening return from Uruguay. Free time in Montevideo depends on the return sailing schedule, not an hour chosen freely by the traveler.

### Why re-entry into Argentina matters

In a single day, a traveler actually leaves Argentina, enters Uruguay, leaves Uruguay and enters Argentina again. Therefore, **re-entry rights and travel documents must be checked in advance**, even though the hotel remains in Buenos Aires throughout. Rules vary by nationality; visa-free entry on one passport does not automatically establish the right to re-enter on a different passport.

For the ferry, travelers need a suitable, valid international passport, a ticket, booking details and documents supporting entry where applicable. Extra time is particularly valuable when the next stages are tightly scheduled: a flight from Buenos Aires to Santiago de Chile is planned for the following day.

## How the journey reaches Bolivia

### First Santiago and the Atacama

After Montevideo, the itinerary continues with a flight from Argentina to Chile, sightseeing in Santiago and a flight to Calama. A ground transfer takes travelers to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), where an overnight stop is planned before the high-altitude crossing. An astronomy excursion can be booked as an optional extra, but it is **not automatically included** in the main itinerary and depends on operating conditions.

This is the actual travel connection between Uruguay's port and Bolivia's lagoons: **not a direct "Montevideo–Uyuni" flight**, but an onward itinerary through Buenos Aires and Chile. Evaluate it using the actual nights and dates; otherwise, the number of transfers may come as a surprise.

### Then the high-altitude lagoons, Uyuni and La Paz

On day 13, **November 3, 2026**, the group begins a 4×4 trip from Chile across the Bolivian border. The itinerary includes Laguna Verde, the Dali Desert, Polques hot springs, Sol de Manana and Laguna Colorada. The following day continues past other lagoons and the Chiguana Salt Flat to Uyuni. The overnight stay in the highlands is at an expedition-style hotel. The guide on the jeep section speaks English.

Later come a flight to [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), the Valley of the Moon and a journey via ancient [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) toward Peru. This is a fairly intensive mountain section. It does not provide several days of relaxation in one resort and calls for different preparation than the visit to Montevideo.

| Stage | What happens |
|---|---|
| Uruguay, October 30 | Montevideo in one day, ferry |
| Argentina and Chile | Return to Buenos Aires, flights, Atacama |
| Bolivia, November 3–6 | Lagoons, Uyuni, La Paz, Tiwanaku |

This combination works well for travelers who intend to see the whole extended itinerary, but **it is disproportionately long for a separate visit to just two countries**. A shorter trip must be planned around flight connections rather than by simply removing neighboring sightseeing days.

## When to travel: two weather challenges, not one season

In Montevideo, late October is spring in the Southern Hemisphere. Coastal winds, possible rain and changeable conditions can noticeably affect a walk around the port and historic neighborhoods. A light windbreaker and closed-toe shoes are useful. When arranging the ferry, monitor the current timetable and the carrier's weather advisories.

In Bolivia's highlands, nights can be cold even under clear sunshine, with strong winds and intense solar radiation. Sections of the route lie **above 4,000 meters**. A light city outfit is not enough: pack warm layers, a hat and protection from the wind and sun. Check temperatures and chances of rain for the specific lagoons and dates, rather than relying on the forecast for La Paz.

Travel between these two regions involves several flights. An adaptable wardrobe makes the change of climate easier: light city clothes, insulation for the highlands, spare socks, comfortable shoes and a small day bag. Luggage size needs to comply with the actual domestic airlines' rules and the luggage space in the jeep.

## Altitude and well-being in Bolivia

The main medical difference between Bolivia and Uruguay is **the high elevation**. Fitness helps on the two-day plateau journey but cannot by itself prevent altitude sickness. Climbing to higher elevations can cause headaches, weakness, nausea and sleep disturbances. Severe cases require stopping the ascent and seeking medical assistance.

The current itinerary includes time in San Pedro de Atacama before departing for Bolivia. This helps prepare the transition to higher elevations but does not guarantee full acclimatization. If you have cardiovascular or respiratory illnesses, difficulty tolerating altitude, or plan to travel with children, discuss the conditions with a doctor and the organizer beforehand.

Medical insurance should match the actual trip: multiple countries, high-altitude vehicle journeys, potential evacuation and long flights. Check the policy and its coverage separately. The tour price alone does not establish that enhanced insurance is included.

## Visas and border crossings: an example for Russian citizens

According to the Consular Department of Russia's Foreign Ministry, as checked on **October 16, 2026**, Bolivia and Uruguay allow short visa-free visits for Russian citizens holding ordinary international passports, **up to 90 days within 180 days** under their respective bilateral agreements. These are two independent legal arrangements, even though the traveler carries one passport.

**Checking only Bolivia and Uruguay is not sufficient for the current tour.** The day trip to Uruguay requires re-entry into Argentina, followed by Chile and a land entry into Bolivia, and then Peru. The remaining countries on the itinerary must also be included in the document checks. Visa rules may differ for travelers of other nationalities, extended stays or non-standard travel purposes.

Before booking, record every leg: entry date, country, mode of transport, departure date, any repeated entry, transit airports and intended length of stay. Check passport validity, return or onward tickets, reservations and airline requirements. Visa-free travel removes a specific visa formality, but authorized border officials make the admission decision.

Ada Tours helps match the actual sequence of countries to each customer's nationality and coordinate road transfers, flights, hotels and excursions. If passport or transit requirements change, the route must be checked again before paying for non-refundable services.

## Currencies and payments on different legs

Uruguay uses the **Uruguayan peso (UYU)**, and Bolivia uses the **boliviano (BOB)**. Between them on this itinerary, travelers also use Argentine pesos (ARS) and Chilean pesos (CLP). Budgeting for small personal expenses should therefore take account of **four successive monetary systems** and the onward route through Peru, Ecuador and Colombia, not just the two country names in the catalog.

US dollars may be useful as a reserve, but acceptance and exchange rates depend on the location. A foreign-issued bank card does not guarantee successful payment to every merchant either, and Russian-issued cards face separate restrictions. Check the bank, payment system, fees, cash-withdrawal limits and payment options with carriers in advance.

On the Montevideo day trip, included ferry tickets already cover some expenses, but personal purchases and meals outside the listed services remain the traveler's responsibility. On the Bolivian plateau, discuss which stops and payments are actually included: not every remote location accepts cards.

## Price and included services

The current 32-day tour lists 4-star hotels, domestic flights, ground transfers, main excursions and entry tickets according to the itinerary. **The Buenos Aires–Montevideo–Buenos Aires ferry is included.** The Montevideo excursion has an English-speaking guide, as does the Bolivian jeep section. Guides' languages differ in the other cities and countries on the tour.

International flights, optional excursions, meals not listed, tips and personal expenses are excluded from that list. The itinerary's stated dates are **October 22–November 22, 2026**. For specific accommodation arrangements and the current price, compare the main tour details:

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

**If you want to spend several days in Uruguay and visit Bolivia without continuing through eight countries, that itinerary needs a separate quotation.** The collection shows current programs with these geographical elements, but it does not itself confirm a ready-made short package covering only the two countries. For an extended Bolivian trip, see [Bolivia's geography and tours](/bolivia/); for urban and coastal travel, explore [Uruguay](/uruguay/) and [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/).

For a different geographical combination, compare [Bolivia and Ecuador](/multi-country/bolivia_ecuador/), which includes the Galapagos Islands, or [Bolivia and Colombia](/multi-country/bolivia_colombia/), which shifts the emphasis to several cities in the Caribbean and Andean regions. In every case, check the actual tour contents: country-combination pages can overlap because they refer to the same long journey.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is there a ready-made tour covering only Bolivia and Uruguay?

The current collection includes a multi-country itinerary passing through both countries; it does not automatically imply a short two-country program. The published 32-day tour includes six other countries. A trip limited to Bolivia and Uruguay requires a separately agreed route and price.

### Do you need to stay overnight in Uruguay to see Montevideo?

Not on the current tour. A day trip by ferry from Buenos Aires, sightseeing and a return to the Argentine hotel are scheduled. To stay overnight, both the itinerary and tickets must be changed.

### Are ferry tickets included in the tour price?

Yes. The 32-day program includes ferry tickets for the Montevideo excursion. That does not mean personal shopping or every extra excursion in Uruguay is included.

### How do travelers reach Bolivia from Uruguay on this itinerary?

After returning from Montevideo to Buenos Aires, travelers fly to Santiago, then Calama, transfer to San Pedro de Atacama and cross the Bolivian border in off-road vehicles. No direct Uruguay–Bolivia flight is included in the published itinerary.

### Do Russian tourists need visas for Uruguay and Bolivia?

According to Russia's Foreign Ministry information as of October 16, 2026, short tourist visits with an ordinary Russian international passport are visa-free for up to 90 days within 180 days. Documents and permitted stays must nevertheless be checked separately for all other countries actually visited, including re-entry into Argentina.

### Which is more difficult on this journey: the ferry or Bolivia?

For the ferry, the main challenges are timing, boarding and borders. Bolivia adds altitude, long jeep journeys and weather conditions. The risks differ; both legs require thoughtful scheduling and enough time.

## What adventures bring Bolivia and Uruguay together?

This collection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The [20-day journey through six countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) visits Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Peru. The [extended 32-day tour of eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) adds Ecuador and Colombia.

The countries in the catalog title do not appear next to each other in the itinerary: Argentina and Chile lie between [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) and Bolivia. The Uruguayan day features sightseeing in the capital and a return ferry to Buenos Aires; the expedition-style adventure takes place in Bolivia. These programs do not promise separate treks, rafting or off-road tours in Uruguay.

## Bolivia: two days on Altiplano roads

After San Pedro de Atacama in Chile, the group crosses the Bolivian border. In 4×4 vehicles, travelers head to Laguna Verde and Licancabur Volcano, through the Dali Desert, Polques hot springs and the geothermal region of Sol de Manana.

[Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) is known for its reddish waters and high-altitude flamingos. Next come the Honda, Hedionda, Chiar Khota and Canapa lagoons, areas near Ollague Volcano and the Chiguana Salt Flat. This section ends at [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). The white salt plain looks different in dry and rainy weather; its mirror effect cannot be guaranteed on any given date.

The route involves long drives and elevations above 4,000 meters. Even without a challenging hike, thinner air can affect travelers' well-being. Acclimatization, warm clothing, sun protection and individual assessment of health are important.

## Uruguay: a city stop on a longer journey

Uruguay is visited from Buenos Aires. A ferry takes travelers to Montevideo, where the itinerary includes the port, Independence Square, the Old Town and the Cathedral. The group then returns to Argentina. This is a substantial cultural excursion and a chance to visit another country, but not an active nature route.

The ferry trip requires a coordinated timetable and enough time for immigration checks. It is particularly important to confirm the right to re-enter Argentina after visiting Uruguay: the rules depend on the traveler's nationality and documents.

## How to choose between 20 and 32 days

| Consideration | Itinerary |
|---|---|
| Fewer travel days | [6 countries in 20 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) |
| Continuation to the Galapagos and Colombia | [8 countries in 32 days](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) |
| Jeep travel in Bolivia | Both itineraries |
| Montevideo | Both itineraries |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026,tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

The longer tour adds new countries, not extra days of extreme adventure in Uruguay. Compare the included flights, overnight stays and mountain guiding arrangements. Other related options are listed among [Bolivia adventure tours](/interests/adventure/tours/bolivia/) and [multi-country adventures](/multi-country/interests/adventure/).

## Climate, equipment and distances

Clothes for city walking are suitable in Montevideo, whereas Bolivia's plateau calls for warm layers, closed-toe shoes and wind protection. Altitude and intense sunlight deserve attention even on a cool day. Access to particular areas depends on road conditions and the weather.

Bolivia uses the boliviano and Uruguay the Uruguayan peso. As the journey also includes several other countries, plan cash and payment methods for each country separately. Neither acceptance of a particular bank's card nor access to cash exchange can be guaranteed without checking.

Russian citizens and travelers of other nationalities must check the entry requirements for each country on the full route and for transit airports separately. Ada Tours helps coordinate the sequence of transfers, border-crossing times and practical details. Insurance coverage and any extra activities are defined by the chosen tour, not the name of the travel theme.

## Frequently asked questions about Bolivia and Uruguay

### Can I see the salt flat without a long hike?

Yes. On these tours, the high-altitude section takes place in 4×4 vehicles with stops along the way. However, the considerable elevation and long drives still require preparation.

### Where is there more adventure, in Bolivia or Uruguay?

On the specific itineraries offered, adventure activities are concentrated in Bolivia. Uruguay is represented by sightseeing in Montevideo.

### Are flamingos and Uyuni's mirror reflections guaranteed?

No. Birds move freely, while water reflections on the salt flat depend on the season and weather.

### Why is there no direct transfer from Uruguay to Bolivia?

The routes include Argentina and Chile. The planned Bolivian jeep section begins in the Atacama.

## What can you learn about the history of Bolivia and Uruguay on one journey?

In [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), travelers discover the history of an Atlantic port city: old neighborhoods, city squares, the Cathedral and the waterfront of the Rio de la Plata. In [Bolivia](/bolivia/), the cultural story moves to a high-altitude plateau where monuments of the Tiwanaku civilization have survived from long before today's South American states existed. These are two different historical narratives that can be compared during the same journey.

The collection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} in which both countries form part of the main route and culture and history are among the principal themes. **These are six- or eight-country journeys, not a single uninterrupted tour limited to Bolivia and Uruguay.** Time at historical sites should therefore be assessed from the daily itinerary, while overall logistics require examining the entire route. For geographical comparison without a thematic filter, see [all tours visiting Bolivia and Uruguay](/multi-country/bolivia_uruguay/).

## Uruguay: one day in historic Montevideo

Both matching itineraries visit Uruguay on a ferry trip from [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) across the Rio de la Plata, returning to Argentina. On arrival, a tour of [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) includes the port, Independence Square, the historic center, Old Town and the Cathedral.

This day offers an understanding of how the city developed beside the great estuary and how its quieter urban environment differs from Buenos Aires. However, **a one-day visit is not an in-depth exploration of all Uruguay's museums and cities**. To see Colonia del Sacramento, visit wineries or stay on the coast, a different itinerary would need to be designed.

The ferry schedule also matters on a historically focused journey. Travel, border procedures and the return departure take up part of the day. The possibility of additional visits depends on the precise sailing times, so the main value should be the advertised sightseeing excursion, rather than an assumption that every city monument can be visited.

## Bolivia: La Paz and the legacy of Tiwanaku

The Bolivian stage begins after [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) in Chile. The itinerary first crosses high-altitude lagoons and salt flats by jeep, then reaches [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and includes a flight to [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/). Cultural stops are not scheduled on every consecutive day: the nature-focused expedition precedes the city and archaeology experiences.

In La Paz, the program includes a city tour with historical sites and the Witches' Market. This provides an opportunity to learn about local traditions, the layout of a highland city and the coexistence of different cultures. The Valley of the Moon is also included, but it is mainly a natural landform and should not be classified as an archaeological monument.

The next cultural stop is [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/), an archaeological complex near Lake Titicaca. Travelers see the Gate of the Sun and Kalasasaya Temple. UNESCO lists Tiwanaku as evidence of the political and religious center of a pre-Hispanic Andean civilization. If archaeology is the priority, devote energy and attention to this visit rather than treating it as a brief stop on the way to Peru.

## Why the country sequence matters for cultural travel

On the [20-day six-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/), Montevideo comes before Santiago and the Atacama, while La Paz and Tiwanaku follow the high-altitude jeep section. The [32-day eight-country route](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) keeps this sequence, then continues through Peru, Ecuador and Colombia.

Experiencing both Uruguayan and Bolivian history therefore involves **other substantial travel stages between them**. There is no direct transfer from Montevideo to La Paz between the visits. Organization involves the ferry between Argentina and Uruguay, flights, a road crossing between Chile and Bolivia and onward travel toward Peru.

There is also a physical contrast: the port city of Montevideo is at sea level, while Tiwanaku lies on a high-altitude plateau. Before visiting Bolivia's monuments, the itinerary passes through regions several thousand meters above sea level. Consider pace, sleep, exertion and any altitude-related medical contraindications before selecting the journey, especially if the archaeological excursion is your main reason for traveling.

## Which itinerary to choose for history

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026,tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

**The 20-day itinerary** suits travelers who want to combine Montevideo, Tiwanaku and other South American highlights without continuing to the Galapagos and Colombia. It also includes Buenos Aires' historic districts and Inca monuments in Peru.

**The 32-day itinerary** broadens the historical geography: after Bolivia and Peru come [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/), [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) and [Bogota](/colombia/place/bogota/). If Bolivia's and Uruguay's culture alone interests you, the longer version does not automatically provide more time in those two countries; the added days are primarily spent elsewhere.

For a journey focused more deeply on Andean heritage, see [cultural tours in Bolivia](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/bolivia/). Travelers more interested in Uruguayan history and architecture can consult the [cultural itineraries through Uruguay](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/uruguay/) and check the specific visiting days.

## Practical decisions before selecting a program

Confirm the visiting sequence, number of nights and mandatory excursions. Montevideo's main limitation is the length of the day trip; for Tiwanaku, it is the altitude and the archaeological visit's place within a busy Andean stage. There is no universal "best season" for both types of cultural tour: check weather conditions for the actual dates, elevations and regions of the complete journey.

Ada Tours helps align the itinerary with your vacation length and preferred historic sites, arrange sensible connections and verify the travel documents required for each guest's nationality. Entry requirements for Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and the other countries on the route are considered separately; the common thematic collection cannot replace those checks.

## Frequently asked questions about Bolivia's and Uruguay's culture

### Can I visit both countries without the other South American countries?

That can be discussed as a custom itinerary. The ready-made tours in this collection include additional countries, so they should not be described as a direct two-country journey.

### What does the historic part of Uruguay include?

On the approved itineraries, it is a one-day sightseeing tour of Montevideo, including the port, Independence Square, Old Town and the Cathedral. An overnight stay in Uruguay is not a required part of this stage.

### Where can travelers discover Bolivia's pre-Hispanic culture?

The principal archaeological visit is [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/), featuring the Gate of the Sun and Kalasasaya Temple. A city tour of La Paz gives a different, more contemporary cultural context.

### Does altitude matter for the Tiwanaku excursion?

Yes. The archaeological complex is on a high plateau, and several preceding days are spent in Andean areas. Assess health and agree on a manageable travel pace before booking.

### Does the 32-day route include more historical excursions in Bolivia and Uruguay?

It primarily adds new countries and cultural sites outside this pair. To compare how thoroughly Bolivia and Uruguay themselves are explored, compare their individual itinerary days rather than the overall tour length.

## Bolivia and Uruguay: food experiences within a six-country journey

Our [Bolivia–Uruguay food and wine collection](/multi-country/bolivia_uruguay/interests/food-and-wine/) includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. It is based on a [20-day tour of six countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/): Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Peru. Food and wine is a theme of the wider itinerary. **It does not mean that dedicated tastings are scheduled in Uruguay or Bolivia.**

Travelers first discover Rio and Iguazu Falls, then Buenos Aires and Montevideo. From Argentina, the route continues to Chile, followed by Bolivia's high-altitude section, before concluding in Peru.

## Montevideo: a brief introduction to Uruguay

Travelers arrive in [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) by ferry from Buenos Aires. The itinerary includes the port, Independence Square, Old Town and the Cathedral. There is free time before the return ferry.

Uruguay is known for its wine production, particularly red Tannat wines, and for the tradition of grilling meat over an open fire. However, **no winery visit is scheduled on this day**. A proper wine-tasting excursion would require additional time and therefore a change to the established itinerary. If you want to try Uruguayan dishes in a restaurant, coordinate lunch with the excursion and ferry schedule.

## Bolivia: Uyuni, lagoons and local cuisine

After crossing the border from Chile, a jeep expedition begins through Laguna Verde, geothermal areas and Laguna Colorada. Travelers then visit [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), Colchani and Incahuasi Island. After the expedition, the route continues through La Paz and Tiwanaku.

Quinoa, corn and potatoes are common ingredients in Andean cuisine. To experience local dishes, select stops that allow enough time for a restaurant. Bolivia's expedition days are devoted to nature and long transfers. The high-altitude section passes above 4,000 meters and calls for attention to acclimatization.

## Where a tasting is actually offered

During the stay in Santiago, Chile, we offer **an optional paid visit to wineries in the Maipo Valley**. This separate option must be arranged before travel. It is the clearest dedicated food-and-wine component of the wider itinerary.

| Country | What is included |
|---|---|
| Uruguay | One day in Montevideo |
| Chile | Maipo Valley wineries, optional extra |
| Bolivia | La Paz, lagoons, Uyuni |

If vineyards are the main goal, consider allowing additional time in Chile or Uruguay. If Uyuni is the main dream, keep the full high-altitude section and plan food experiences around the available free hours.

## How to plan a food-focused extension

We help coordinate the sequence of countries, transport, accommodation and possible extra visits. A winery excursion or a special restaurant day must be agreed separately; neither should be regarded as included just because the tour has a food-and-wine theme. You can also compare [other food and wine journeys](/interests/food-and-wine/) and [all multi-country tours](/multi-country/).

## Frequently asked questions

### Is a wine tasting in Uruguay included in the base itinerary?

No. A sightseeing tour of Montevideo and free time before the ferry are included.

### Can I add a winery visit?

Yes, this can be discussed when customizing the itinerary. Uruguay would require extra time and transport; in Chile, Maipo wineries are already listed as a separate paid option.

### Is Bolivia the wine-focused stage of this tour?

No. The Bolivian section visits high-altitude lagoons, the Uyuni Salt Flat and La Paz. No wine tasting is listed for this part.

### Is one day enough to experience Montevideo's food?

Possibly for a restaurant if free time permits. For winery visits, it is better to schedule additional time in advance.

## Bolivia and Uruguay on one journey: the ocean shore and the Altiplano

Our collection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Both itineraries feature Bolivia and Uruguay as parts of a much wider South American trip. However, **Uruguay is represented by a single day in Montevideo**, while Bolivia involves several days in jeeps among high-altitude lagoons and the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/).

These nature experiences cannot be compared by applying one checklist of attractions. In [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), visitors see the broad water horizon of the Rio de la Plata, the waterfront, the port and the historic center. The Bolivian segment starts at mountain crossings from Chile and includes lagoons, geothermal regions and dry salt plains at high elevation.

The logistics also differ considerably: Uruguay is visited from Buenos Aires by crossing the Rio de la Plata, while Bolivia comes after the [Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) on a high-altitude 4×4 route. No direct, quick transfer connects the two countries on the current itineraries.

## 20 days: six countries from Rio to Machu Picchu

The [6 Countries of Latin America in 20 Days tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) connects Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Peru. Travelers start in Rio de Janeiro, then visit both sides of [Iguazu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and Buenos Aires.

The Uruguayan section is a [Montevideo sightseeing excursion](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) featuring the port, Independence Square, the Old Town and the Cathedral. Buenos Aires–Montevideo–Buenos Aires ferry tickets are listed as included services. This is a full day exploring the capital, but not a separate multi-day tour of Uruguay's beaches and nature parks.

After flights and transfers through Chile, the itinerary reaches Bolivia's highlands. Here travelers encounter [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), the [Salvador Dali Desert](/bolivia/place/salvador-dali-desert/), thermal areas, colorful lagoons and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). The journey continues to La Paz and then Peru.

The central natural challenge is the contrast between the warm, low-lying coast and elevations above 4,000 meters in parts of Bolivia. The high-altitude sections carry a risk of altitude sickness, which should be discussed in advance.

## 32 days: more countries, a similar high-altitude stage

The [8 Countries of South America in 32 Days tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) adds Ecuador and Colombia to the broader route. The trip also begins through Brazil and Argentina, and Uruguay is again visited on a day excursion from Buenos Aires to Montevideo, returning by ferry.

The Bolivian segment includes [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), the [Sol de Manana geysers](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/), [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), the Uyuni Salt Flat, [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) and [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/). It also uses jeeps, with an overnight stay in an expedition-style highland hotel.

The main difference between the tours is overall duration and what comes afterward: the 32-day version includes the Galapagos Islands and Colombian cities. Do not choose the longer option solely for Uruguay; the Uruguayan section remains short on both itineraries.

## Altitude and climate matter more than the difference in tour length

[Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) lies on a high plateau. Parts of the route rise above 4,000 meters. A traveler accustomed to the lowland climate of Uruguay or Brazil's coast may feel the altitude even with good physical fitness. Do not self-prescribe preventive medication; if you have heart or lung disease or other risk factors, discuss the itinerary with a doctor before booking.

Mornings and nights can be cold at altitude, while solar radiation is stronger. Uruguay's coast and summer days in Buenos Aires can be much warmer. Pack several clothing layers, wind and sun protection, comfortable shoes for walks and compact day luggage.

In dry months, the salt flat often reveals its white salt surface; after rain, some sections may have a thin layer of water reflecting the sky. Water conditions and route access depend on the weather, however, so a mirror-like surface cannot be promised for a particular day. Local conditions determine road access and whether lagoons can be visited.

## Visas, money and flights: guidance for Russian citizens

As of **October 21, 2026**, the Russian Foreign Ministry confirms visa-free entry into Bolivia for Russian citizens for up to 90 days within each 180-day period. Uruguay's Interior Ministry official list also identifies holders of ordinary Russian passports as travelers who do not need to obtain a tourist visa in advance. These rules depend on the relevant citizenship and purpose of entry; they do not replace checks on transit and other requirements of the full itinerary.

Both tours include countries beyond Bolivia and Uruguay. Documents must therefore be checked **for each entry and transit separately**, taking into account passport validity, airports, airlines and the actual order of border crossings. We can help compile a sequential checklist, but visa-free arrangements do not guarantee admission at the border.

Bolivia's main currency is the boliviano (BOB), and Uruguay's is the Uruguayan peso (UYU). Plan cash for personal expenses, exchange fees and payments in intermediate countries in advance. Do not assume that a Russian-issued bank card will work on every leg: check actual payment access before traveling.

On both 20-day and 32-day tours, connections and luggage need coordination because ferries, domestic flights, jeeps and intercity transfers impose different requirements. The ferry journey does not eliminate immigration checks on the Argentine and Uruguayan borders; the high-altitude vehicle crossing into Bolivia is also a separate international border stage.

## Who should choose a Bolivia and Uruguay combination?

This combination is primarily for people who want to experience **a broad sweep of South America on one journey**, rather than only two countries. Uruguay offers the contrast of a relaxed coastal city after Buenos Aires, while Bolivia provides a longer nature stage with lagoons, desert and salt flats.

If the goal is specifically Uruguay's national parks and ocean coast, the itinerary would need an extension because the current tours spend just one day in the country. If you want more time on the Altiplano, focus on the number of Bolivian days, elevations and overnight accommodation conditions.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do these tours include several days in Uruguay?

No. On both itineraries discussed, Uruguay is represented by a one-day excursion from Buenos Aires to Montevideo.

### Where is the richest nature-focused section of this pair?

In Bolivia's highlands: lagoons, thermal areas, the Dali Desert and Uyuni occupy several days.

### Can altitude cause problems?

Yes. The routes include elevations above 4,000 meters, where altitude sickness is a risk. Individual assessment of physical demands and acclimatization is important before traveling.

### Do Russian citizens need separate visas for Bolivia and Uruguay?

As of October 21, 2026, official references indicate visa-free tourist entry for Russian citizens to both countries. Other countries, transit, passports and carrier rules must be checked separately.
